H1.claim: Intermediate layers beat the last layer (E1 proposal).
H1.expect: NOT supported: last_norm is best or within tol of the best intermediate layer (pilot: block 8 was -0.032).
H1.rule: supported if best-by-val intermediate beats last_norm (real); refuted if last_norm beats it (real); else inconclusive. Judged on M1 and M2.

H2.claim: The gap fine-tuning minus linear probing grows with the number of labelled images.
H2.expect: With <=500 images FT-2 is within tol of LP; with 4000 images FT-2/FT-4 beat LP by >= tol.
H2.rule: supported if delta(N_min) < tol, delta(N_max) real and >= tol, and delta(N_max)-delta(N_min) >= tol (FT-2 vs LP, M1 and M2).

H3.claim: DINOv3 beats DINOv2 as a frozen backbone, but by little because Mars is far from both pretraining sets; both beat random init by a lot.
H3.rule: supported if DINOv3-DINOv2 is real (>= tol) and both beat random by > 0.1.

H4.claim: A 3.5M-param decoder head does not beat a 4.6k-param linear probe at full data on M1/M2 (capacity saturation).
H4.expect: |delta| < tol on M1 and M2; any gain appears only in M3.
H4.rule: supported if the decoder-minus-LP difference on M1 and M2 is not real in favour of the decoder.

H5.claim: Part of the M1/M2 ceiling is label noise at region borders: excluding a band around label edges raises every model and shrinks the spread between models.
H5.expect: mIoU(r=8) - mIoU(r=0) >= 0.03 on M1 for every config, spread across configs smaller at r=8.

H6.claim: big_rock failure is size-driven: small or fragmented boulders are missed, large contiguous ones are found.
H6.expect: Recall of the largest third of big_rock components exceeds the smallest third by >= 0.2.
H6.rule: supported if that gap is >= 0.2 (LP last_norm, pooled M1+M2).
